notes: Cliopatria has no Xhosa row; the Cape dossier names 'Xhosa chiefdoms' (a string, not a slug) as counterpart six times and this slug is the dossier for it. Two pages: Xhosa Wars (every date and land above) and Xhosa people (the kingdom 'founded before the 15th century' by Tshawe; Amatola and Winterberg; Kei and Fish rivers; cattle-killing 1856-1858, which is not a land event). The Xhosa_Kingdom title did not load (URL_NOT_FOUND). The Transkei page was opened and has nothing on the 19th century. The start year 1779 is a bridge (first Xhosa land date), not the founding. Gcalekaland is drawn as a box (Great Kei to Mthatha) since no page gives its boundaries; Tembuland, Fingoland, Griqualand East and Pondoland are outside it. The page does not say the Cape annexed Gcalekaland in 1878-79; the successor is the Cape by the page's 'administered as a British territory'. Counterpart: british-cape-colony (af-07-b), whose events use the string 'Xhosa chiefdoms'. Gazetteer names needed: British Kaffraria (flagged by the Cape dossier too), Gcalekaland, Transkei, Ciskei, Zuurveld, Great Fish (river), Keiskamma (river).
